luna_bala_original_selection.comment: He is lukewarm on this song but called 0:41 great: the five small drum strokes at 41.6-42.2 that lead into the return at 42.35 must be in every cut. The 5.6 s voice pickup and the first drum body can go; the quiet voice break at 35-42 is the calm part, so keep it.

cuts.why: Opens 0.2 s before the bass takes the foreground at 20.28, so the first second is a change rather than a body already running. Then the bass sentences with their drum fills, the bare drums at 33.3, the quiet voice break 35.1-42.3 (loudness drops from 7 to 3), the 0:41 strokes and the whole final return up to the last drum at 57.27. Clear shape: groove, a break, a return. It loses only the opening pickup and the first drum body. 36.9 s.

Near-perfect loop. Opens in the middle of the first drum body (drummer and upper answers), runs through the bass entry at 20.3, the voice break and 0:41, then 7.7 s of the final return. More drums at the start and less of the return than the first cut. It opens on a body already running, not on an event. 36.9 s.

Longest option (44.3 s), with the best match: nearly the whole song after the drums arrive. It holds every section (drum body, bass, voice break, 0:41, final return) but is close to the 45 s limit and repeats the full body twice.

luna_bala_slowed_selection.comment: No cut loops well: the best match is 0.62 and anything that keeps the voice and pickup (where the drums enter at 20.92) is at 0.43 or below. He wants the voice at 12-20 followed differently, so the cut that leaves it out is also the safest for today's spec.

cuts.why: Best loop. Opens 3.5 s into the drums with the upper melody already floating, has the bridge at 36.2-38.4 where the bass vanishes, then the drum and bass duet, the exposed chords after 53.6, and ends just before the new word at 55.79. Loses the voice coming in from a distance and the arrival of the drums. Its shape is mild, a floating line then a duet, with no quiet part. 31.3 s.

The song's real arc: the voice materialising out of near silence (loudness 1-2), the pickup, the drums entering at 20.92, the upper melody, the bridge and the start of the duet. Best shape, but a weak loop, and it opens on a near-silent voice, a poor first two seconds. It also contains 12-20, the passage he flagged. 34.9 s.

Starts as the sung sentence stops, so the first 5 s are the faster pickup building into the drums at 20.92; then the melody, the bridge and most of the duet. A more urgent opening than the second cut, but the loop is weak and 15.5-20 is still in the flagged passage. 37.1 s.

montagem_coma_selection.comment: He called it pure banger, and earlier said 'the passage at 0:27 is just awesome' (the rap in the second drum hole at 27.6-28.6). Every cut keeps 0:27. The music is two near-identical burst cycles, so one cycle plus the voice foreground at 33.6-43 is enough. Several cuts loop near-perfectly.

cuts.why: Perfect loop. Opens on the second burst cycle, the 0:27 rap arrives 2.6 s in, then the held-voice foreground at 33.6-43 (the calm part: bass drops, mids rise), and the whole last return with the little vocal bridge at 50 s, up to the end. Groove, rap, voice, groove: a clear shape. Loses the first cycle and the light upper figure, which repeat what is kept. 32 s.

Opens inside the opening drum bursts (strong), then the light upper figure at 9.6-15 (calm), the voice answers, the return at 19.07, 0:27, the voice foreground and the last return up to the 50 s vocal bridge. Most variety, but 44 s long, and it plays the burst cycle twice.

Same core as the first cut (0:27, the voice foreground, the last return) but it starts 2 s after the return at 19.07 and ends 4 s earlier, just after the vocal bridge. Use it if the 57 s ending feels too long. 32 s.

montagem_tomada_extended_selection.comment: The song is two cycles of voice, swell and return (0-25 and 25.6-55). One cycle and one return are enough. He found 0-11 and 33-40 weak (the voice should be followed more ambitiously), so the first cut avoids 0-11. No cut also avoids 33-40, because that is the build into the final return.

cuts.why: Opens in the first return's drums and upper figure, then the quiet second voice passage at 25.6-33 (loudness falls to 3), the pickup and last swell at 35-40, and the final drum and voice duet from 40.55 to 53.2. Full calm-to-intense shape and a near-perfect loop. It keeps the 33-40 passage he called weak. 36.9 s.

Exactly one cycle: 1.2 s of drums, the voice again at 25.6, pickup, swell, the final return and the real ending at 55.32 with its decay, which then loops back into the drums. The tightest shape (31.4 s). The quiet voice comes within 2 s, so the opening is short on punch.

A different shape: opens on the voice in its first cycle (inside the 0-11 passage he called weak), the swell, the whole first return, the second voice passage, and it ends inside the pickup before the final return. The video loops on anticipation instead of a climax. Good match, but it misses the vocal duet return. 31.4 s.

montagem_tomada_slowed_selection.comment: His note is general ('good, could be more ambitious'). The music has a clear valley: voice in space at 21-31 (loudness 2-3), the build at 31-39, the big return at 39.49. A cut should cross that valley and reach the return. The drum phrases at 0-11 can go. Excellent loops are available.

cuts.why: Opens on the last 2 s of the groove (drums and upper duet), drops into the voice in space at 21, the upper breath, the bass build and the held word at 37.86 into the return at 39.49, then 14 s of the final body. Groove, quiet, build, release in 35 s: the best shape.

Adds the drums with light answers and the full groove before the voice, so more drums first, with the same valley and return. 43.9 s, longer than he leans toward. It opens on drum phrases, which is a solid but not striking hook.

Starts with the voice already in space (a quiet, intimate opening, weaker in the first 2 s), runs through the build and return and ends on the last upper approach just before the release at 57.04. Calm first, intense second, so the shape is clear, but the loop jumps from the full body straight into the bare voice. 35.1 s.

montagem_tomada_super_slowed_selection.comment: The voice section (17-35, loudness 2-3) is the calm part and the drum return at 37.01 is the event. Both should be in, and the long light-figure opening can go. Matches are near-perfect.

cuts.why: Opens on the last 4 s of the body (drums, so a firm opening), then the singer takes flight at 17.35, the vocal breath and upper turns at 23-26, the gathering turns and swell, the drum return at 37.01 with the singer over every drum, and 16 s of it. Body, quiet, return. 39.4 s.

Starts 0.4 s before the voice at 17.35, so the first moment is the call. It gets more of the return, up to the last upper turns before the final kick at 56.73. Same length (39.4 s) as the first, with a quieter opening and a fuller end.
Shorter (34.5 s): 7 s of body, the voice section, the swell and only 7.7 s of the return. It leaves the return just as it settles, so the climax is brief.

no_batidao_selection.comment: Great apart from the opening (until ~0:08 he wants the voice followed), which a cut must start after anyway. The bass arriving at 15.24 is the hook. The best loops start late and miss it; the cut that opens on it loops only decently (0.73).

cuts.why: Opens 1.2 s before the bass arrives at 15.24, so the first two seconds are the end of the drum build hitting the drop: the strongest possible opening. Then the upper-melody body, the low singer with sparse drums at 29.55, the four-stroke handoff at ~44 and the drummer alone. Ends before the last soft strokes. 40.6 s, at the top of his range.

Near-perfect loop. Opens mid-body (bass and upper melody running), then the low-singer passage at 29.55 (the calmer part), the last body and the end. Misses the drop at 15.24, so the opening is a groove already going rather than an event. 36.9 s.

The whole drum build from its start (loudness 4), the drop at 15.24, the body, the singer, and the handoff into the drummer's last body. The strongest shape (build, drop, contrast) and it skips the weak opening, but the first 7 s are the build, a slower hook, and the loop is only fair. 38.8 s.

no_batidao_slowed_selection.comment: He rates it 'a very good specification overall, so rhythmic', so there is no weak passage to avoid. The voice section at 23.6-32.5 is the only calm part and the return at 32.5 is the release. Both should be in. The bass arriving at 6.41 is the best opening but loops less well.

cuts.why: Opens in the full bass body, then the new low singer over sparse drums at 23.63 (calm), the return at 32.5, the roll at 41.1-41.7 and the last upper and drum duet. Body, voice, return, roll: good shape, near-perfect loop. 37.7 s.
2.6 s of body, then the voice, the return and the roll, ending on the three ending turns past 58.58. More of the late duet and the real ending, less of the first body. 37.75 s.
Opens 0.4 s before the bass arrives at 6.41, the strongest first two seconds the song offers. The whole first body, the voice, the return and the roll, ending at 44.3. Loop only fair. 38.3 s.

passo_bem_solto_selection.comment: Great overall; he wants the voice at 9-24 followed better and 37-39 improved. Loudness is nearly flat across the song (6-7), so the shape comes from changes of foreground (voice, drum answers, upper figure, five naked calls, full return), not from quiet and loud. The 0.73-1.03 matches mean loops are easy.

cuts.why: Perfect loop at his preferred length (36.9 s). Opens 0.3 s before the vocal response at 9.11 (the sub bass drops, so it is the song's calmer stretch), then the drum answers, the upper-figure return at 24.08, the five naked calls at 37.2-38.65 and 7 s of the last return. Every foreground is there, but the opening 15 s are the vocal passage he says the spec under-follows. Best if that passage gets reworked.

Opens 0.3 s after the drum answers at 18.54, so it skips most of the weak vocal passage. Then the return, the naked calls and the whole last return with its taper to the end. Fair loop, 36.9 s. Less contrast: no real voice-led section.
Shortest (31.4 s): 1.9 s of drum answers into the return at 24.08, the calls and the last return. Two returns with only the 1.5 s of calls between them, so the shape is flat.

passo_bem_solto_slowed_selection.comment: A 'banger' except 0:08-0:12, where the spec does not follow the voice. The bass and low-voice conversation at 17.1-23.3 is a distinct calmer colour worth keeping. The return at 23.31 and the naked call at 37.6-40 into the last return are the core.

cuts.why: Opens inside the low conversation (bass foreground, the lower voice climbing from 19.66), 2.6 s before the return at 23.31. Then the full drums with the measured B3 turns, the exposed call at 38-40 and the drum and bass last return. Avoids the weak 8-12 passage. Good loop, 33.2 s.
Perfect loop: the whole sung sentence from 6.5, the bass conversation, the return, the call and 7.7 s of the last return. The fullest shape, but it contains 8-12 (weak spec today) and is 41.5 s long.
Like the first cut but starts 0.7 s into the bass foreground at 17.1, so the whole low conversation with its four drum answers is kept as the calm opening. Fair loop, 35.2 s.

passo_bem_solto_super_slowed_selection.comment: Same remark as Passo: the voice section (5.5-23) is under-followed. Calls at 38.9-40.6, then the last return. The return at 23.25 keeps the sung C4 as foreground with sparse drums, so contrast inside the song is mild in loudness (flat 6-7).

cuts.why: Opens on the high answers (16.7-18.4 just passed) and the low reply with five strong drum marks, then the change of accompaniment at 23.25, the five naked calls at 38.9-40.6 and 14 s of the last return. Skips the under-followed voice section. Good loop, 35.1 s.

The whole sung sentence from 1 s in, the answers, the return, the calls and 10 s of the last return. Best loop and the most complete shape, but 43.9 s long and it opens on the passage he finds weakly followed.

A middle option: starts at the long F3 at 8.74 (already sung), keeps the rest of the voice section and answers, the return and calls, and ends 5.7 s into the last return. 37.3 s, good loop, but it opens mid-sentence.

petrunko_selection.comment: What makes it work is the single 20 s acceleration from 1.3 s (barely audible ticks) to the roll at 19.8, the 1.4 s suspension and the return at 22.4. A cut must start at 6 s or later and then hold 20+ s of replies, so no 30-45 s cut keeps the whole build: the best keeps its audible half (drum hits from 11.5) and loses the faint ticks at the start, which carry its slowness. Every cut that keeps the build loops weakly (0.22-0.44). Plainly: a short is a lesser version of this one.

cuts.why: Opens on the first build hit at 11.48: 8 s of build (hits, then doubles), the roll, the suspension, the return at 22.4 and 24 s of replies. It keeps everything audible of the build, which the faint tick half (1.3-11.5, loudness 3) is not. Weak loop: the end, mid-replies, does not lead in step into the build. 35.1 s.

Opens on the doubled hits 3 s before the roll, so the build is only a short ramp. Keeps the full aftermath including the five-stroke decay to the end (loop from the decay back into the doubles is the best of these, still only fair). 43.3 s.
Between the two: 5 s of build before the roll, the suspension, the return and 27 s of replies, ending before the decay. 34.4 s, weak loop.

tiki_tiki_48s.comment: Keeping it whole is worse than a cut: at 48 s it is over the limit, and its first 7 s (quiet support intro, loudness 1) and last 6 s (float out) are slow for a short. The drop hook at 10.43 is the obvious opening. All loops are weak (0.39 at best); he has left no note on this song.

cuts.why: Opens 0.1 s before the first hard drop at 10.43, the strongest possible first moment. Then the hook body, the reset at 24.35 (the dip, loudness 2-3), the run at 27.83 and the first 2.5 s of the float out. Drop, breath, run: a clear shape. Weak loop. 33.9 s.

Almost the whole song minus the quiet intro: it opens on the first beats at 6.9, builds 3.5 s into the drop, and ends at the close of the float out, so it loops from fading to sparse beats, which may feel natural even though the rhythm match is weak. 40.8 s.
Same opening on the first beats, but it leaves the float out after 2 s, so the loop goes from the run's tail back into the beats. 36.4 s.

trouble_50s.comment: Keeping it whole (50 s) is too long and opens with 14.7 s of quiet voice, slow for a short. A cut should open at or near the groove at 14.71 and keep the break at 27.6 and the drop at 29.02 (the peak). He wants the voice at 27-29 followed more ambitiously and bigger impacts at 14-29. All loops are weak (0.37 at best) because the loud final kicks do not match the groove's rhythm.

cuts.why: Opens 0.8 s into the 3-3-2 groove, then the three exposed words at 27.6, the drop and its bass stop-and-go at 29-43.4, the five exposed words with the drum swell, and the six closing kicks. Groove, break, drop, break, kicks: strong shape. Loses the whole voice intro. 34.5 s, weak loop.
Adds the last five intro words gathering pace (12-14.7), so the opening is a lead-in into the groove rather than the groove itself, and it runs to the end. 38 s, weak loop.
Opens 0.8 s before the groove on the last intro words, but ends at 48.4, before the last closing kicks finish. 34.5 s, weak loop.

valhalla_40s.comment: No cut loops: every candidate has a match at or below zero. At 40 s the whole song fits, and its quiet 10 s opening is the anticipation that the drop at 30.06 pays off, so keeping it whole is better than any cut. He prefers the handcrafted current spec, which separates the female and male voices in the phrases at 10-30.

cuts.why: Opens 0.7 s before the phrases section at 9.97, then the alternating voices and the drop groove at 30.06 to near the end. Loses the 10 s opening, so the drop has less build. No rhythmic loop. Only if 40 s is too long. 30.4 s.
Keeps the last 3.6 s of the opening, so it opens quieter and more patiently, then the phrases and drop. No rhythmic loop. 33 s.
